reasons: Opinion supports the holding: officers applying for warrants get qualified, not absolute, immunity ('we hold that the same standard of objective reasonableness that we applied ... in Leon ... defines the qualified immunity'), and immunity is lost where 'no reasonably competent officer would have concluded that a warrant should issue' / 'no officer of reasonable competence would have requested the warrant' (fn.9).

'Loses qualified immunity' where the affidavit is so lacking in probable cause tracks the 'so lacking in indicia of probable cause as to render official belief in its existence unreasonable ... will the shield of immunity be lost' language at *345.

Malley is a foundational qualified-immunity case (source of the 'all but the plainly incompetent or those who knowingly violate the law' formulation) refining Harlow's objective-reasonableness standard; 'Qualified Immunity' home with 'Key — Progeny / Refinement' role is apt and matches frontmatter homes[].
residual_risks: Frontmatter home is '[[Qualified Immunity]]' while the rendered 'Appears on' section lists '[[Section 1983 Liability and Qualified Immunity]]' — a wikilink-target naming inconsistency in the content page, but the assertion payload faithfully tracks the frontmatter home and is doctrinally correct; cannot be adjudicated as a defect from disclosed evidence alone.
